title: Alternate destination clinics for mental health and addictions
subtitle: Restorative justice and the Anti-Hate By-law, plus a Doon Heritage Village utility upgrade update.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee received an update on Alternate Destination Clinics, which would give people in a mental health or addictions crisis somewhere to go other than a hospital emergency room. Partners said the steering committee aims to open two sites, one in each Ontario Health Team area, and will submit a funding application to Ontario Health West. No locations have been chosen yet. The update was received for information, so no decision was needed.

A delegate from a local restorative justice agency asked the committee to build restorative options into implementation of the new Regional Anti-Hate By-law, which takes effect in January. Staff said they would consult restorative justice organizations and share the implementation plan with Council. The minutes also record that the committee discussed extending the by-law's provisions to all area municipalities.
The only recorded vote was on the Consent Agenda {{vote:m1}}. It received the Doon Heritage Village utility upgrade project update for information. The committee's next meeting is January 16, 2024.

decisions.item: Consent Agenda: Doon Heritage Village utility upgrade
decisions.detail: The committee received the Doon Heritage Village utility upgrade project update for information, as part of the Consent Agenda.

debate: The restorative justice delegate argued that punishment alone tends not to change harmful beliefs and can push the behaviour elsewhere. The delegate asked for restorative options to run alongside by-law enforcement, not replace it, and said participation would be voluntary.

Some councillors questioned how this request relates to existing Regional funding for the same organization. Staff said that funding is for a separate Justice Centre and that they would report back on it. They also said restorative justice could be considered for by-law cases.

The Regional Solicitor said restorative justice and the by-law can work in parallel. Staff said training for enforcement officers already covers education and prevention, and that an implementation update would go to Council. One councillor worried the two approaches might conflict. Staff did not see a conflict.

One councillor said the by-law covers only Regional property and wanted a consistent approach across all area municipalities, with a motion to follow later. Another said their city is already drafting its own anti-hate by-law to work alongside the Regional one.

On the clinics, councillors asked about links to existing police and mental health crisis teams, and about walk-in access without referral. Partners said the programs would be linked and that walk-in access is a priority. Paramedic Services said paramedics currently have to take mental health patients to the emergency room. They would need provincial approval to take them to the clinics instead.
